summary: Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Stedelijk Gymnasium Haarlem and Leiden University, later holding posts at the University of Amsterdam (1892–1899) and Leiden University (1899–1926).

Christine Chojnacki specializes in Indology and religious studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1991 and is attested as Professeur at Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 in 2018.

Christine Mollier is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied under Kristofer Schipper. She served as a CNRS researcher (1989–1995) and Director of Research (attested 2006–2014), and held a visiting professorship at the University of Chicago.
Christmas Humphreys worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He was educated at Malvern College and Trinity Hall, Cambridge, and served as President of The Buddhist Society from circa 1924 to 1983.

Christoph Anderl is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned an MA at the University of Vienna and completed his PhD at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Christoph Harbsmeier.

Christoph Cüppers is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, and Albrecht Wezler, and served as Director of the Lumbini International Research Institute (~1993–2013).

Christoph Emmrich works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Heidelberg University, where he held an attested post in 2001, and later became an Assistant Professor at the University of Toronto.

Christoph Harbsmeier specializes in Sinology and linguistics. He studied at Merton College, Oxford, and the University of Copenhagen, and held posts at Universiti Sains Malaysia and the University of Oslo, alongside advisory professorships at Peking, Fudan, and Shanghai Normal universities.

Christoph Kleine works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Marburg and Bukkyo University, he held posts at Marburg, Hōbōgirin, the University of Munich, and Leipzig University.

Christoph Theodosius Walther was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied theology at the University of Halle in 1720 and served as a missionary with the Danish-Halle Mission from circa 1725 to 1740.

Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf worked in Indology, Tibetology, and anthropology. Educated at Vienna and the London School of Economics under Leo Frobenius and Robert von Heine-Geldern, he held posts at Vienna, Osmania University, and the University of London (1950–1976).
Christophe Jaffrelot works in Indology and related fields. He studied at Sciences Po under Jean Leca, completing his studies around 1991, and held posts at Sciences Po and the CNRS around 1991.
Christophe Vielle is an Indologist. He has held positions at UCLouvain, where he is attested as professeur de sanskrit in 2009 and as professeur in 2013.

Christopher Byrne specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at McGill University, where his supervisors and teachers included Grace S. Fong, G. Victor Sōgen Hori, and Robin D. S. Yates.
Christopher D. Emms works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at McMaster University under the doctoral supervision of Shayne Clarke.

Christopher G. Framarin works in philosophy and Indology. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi and a PhD at the University of New Mexico, and was attested as an associate professor at the University of Calgary in 2014.
Christopher Hatchell specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Virginia, where he was mentored by David Germano.

Christopher I. Beckwith works in Tibetology, Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Ohio State and Indiana University under Helmut Hoffmann and Thubten Jigme Norbu, later holding a professorship in Central Eurasian Studies at Indiana University.

Christopher Ives specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He held a post as Assistant Professor of Religion at the University of Puget Sound (~1987–2001) and became professor and chair of religious studies at Stonehill College around 2001.

Christopher Jon Jensen works in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Saskatchewan, Kyoto University, and McMaster University (PhD 2018), where his doctoral supervisor was James A. Benn.
